edges.description: Disrupted ocular morphogenesis produces abnormally small eyes.
Severe disruption of ocular morphogenesis can produce absent globes.
Impaired optic fissure closure and ocular morphogenesis produce chorioretinal and ocular colobomas.
Disrupted neural crest-derived periocular mesenchyme differentiation produces anterior segment dysgenesis with corneal opacity.
Impaired anterior segment morphogenesis in neural crest-derived periocular mesenchyme produces Peters anomaly with iridocorneal and lenticulocorneal adhesions.
Severe anterior segment dysgenesis during RARB-dependent eye morphogenesis can produce aniridia.
Abnormal pulmonary development produces lung underdevelopment.
Abnormal diaphragm formation produces hernia or eventration.
Abnormal cardiac morphogenesis produces congenital heart defects.
Dysregulated retinoid signaling in the brain produces progressive spasticity, dystonia, and chorea.

Disrupted RARB-dependent brain and motor system development produces severe global motor delay.
Disrupted neurodevelopment and oromotor control produce delayed speech and language development.
Disrupted hindbrain and posterior fossa development produces Chiari type I malformation in the majority of survivors.
Disrupted forebrain commissural development produces corpus callosum hypoplasia.
Central neurological and bulbar dysfunction in surviving individuals produces severe feeding difficulties.
Central nervous system dysfunction manifests in infancy and early childhood with marked axial hypotonia.
Disrupted cerebral development predisposes a subset of affected individuals to refractory seizures.

nodes.description: Pathogenic variants in RARB alter the retinoic acid receptor beta protein, a ligand-activated nuclear receptor. De novo dominant missense variants in and around the ligand-binding domain increase ligand-induced transcriptional activity (gain-of-function), biallelic nonsense and frameshift variants abolish receptor activity (recessive loss-of-function), and some heterozygous loss-of-function variants disrupt wild-type receptor function through a dominant-negative effect. Missense variants in the highly conserved DNA-binding domain form a further loss-of-function class, reducing steady-state protein levels and impairing nuclear localization of the receptor.
